title: Work is a signed scalar; only the parallel component changes energy
caution: This applies to a constant force only. d is the displacement of the point of application of the force. A force component perpendicular to the displacement does no work and cannot change the system's energy.
ced_evidence: 3.2.A.3.i: "Only the component of the force exerted on a system that is parallel to the displacement of the point of application of the force will change the system's total energy." 3.2.A.2: "Work is a scalar quantity that may be positive, negative, or zero."

title: Work-energy theorem
caution: The sum is the net work done by all forces exerted on the object.
ced_evidence: 3.2.A.4: "the change in an object's kinetic energy is equal to the sum of the work (net work) being done by all forces exerted on the object."

title: Sign of work: positive when done on the system
body: Work done on a system is positive when it transfers energy into the system and negative when it transfers energy out of the system.
caution: Work can also be zero, for example when the force is perpendicular to the displacement or when there is no displacement of the point of application.
ced_evidence: 3.2.A.1: "Work is the amount of energy transferred into or out of a system by a force"; 3.2.A.2: "may be positive, negative, or zero"

title: Potential energy of a system
body: Potential energy is a scalar quantity associated with the positions of objects within a system, and a system of two or more objects has it only if those objects interact with each other through conservative forces.
ced_evidence: 3.3.A.1: "has potential energy if the objects within that system only interact with each other through conservative forces"; 3.3.A.2: "scalar quantity associated with the position of objects within a system"

title: Energy dissipated by friction
caution: Use the length of the path over which the friction force is exerted, not the net displacement. Friction is nonconservative and its work is path-dependent. The dissipated mechanical energy appears as thermal energy or sound.
ced_evidence: 3.2.A.4.iii: "The energy dissipated by friction is typically equated to the force of friction times the length of the path over which the force is exerted"

title: Zero of potential energy is the observer's choice
body: The definition of zero potential energy for a given system is a decision made by the observer to simplify or otherwise assist in analysis.
ced_evidence: 3.3.A.3: "The definition of zero potential energy for a given system is a decision made by the observer"

title: Which energies a system can have
body: A system of a single object can have only kinetic energy, while a system whose objects interact via conservative forces or that can change shape reversibly may have both kinetic and potential energies.
ced_evidence: 3.4.A.1: "A system composed of only a single object can only have kinetic energy." 3.4.A.2: "interact via conservative forces or that can change its shape reversibly may have both kinetic and potential energies"
